questions.stem: A 32-year-old male with a history of diarrhoea and neurogenic bladder requiring intermittent self-catheterization presents to the clinic with a complaint of a new rash around his groin. On examination, you note a patch of erythematous skin with multiple pustules. A swab of the area grows a gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic bacterium. Considering the patient's medical history and the typical skin flora that can be found in the groin area due to faecal contamination, which organism is most likely responsible for this presentation?
